title: Deletion receipt
description: Every deletion produces a receipt: what was deleted, when, by which method, and who authorized it. Receipts are the proof of deletion for audits and data-subject requests. A deletion without a receipt is treated as unconfirmed. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers what/when/method/authority per deletion.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Overwrite verification
description: After overwrite-based sanitization, the media is read back and checked for the expected pattern. Verification is sampled for large media and complete for small. Failed verification triggers re-sanitization, not acceptance. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers read-back pattern checks.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 64, 2: 256, 3: 1024}
N = CFG[LEVEL]
import random
random.seed(91)
media = bytearray(random.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(N))
pattern = 0x00
for i in range(N): media[i] = pattern  # overwrite
ok = all(b == pattern for b in media)
print("blocks:", N, "| overwrite verified:", ok)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Crypto-shredding
description: When data is encrypted, destroying the key renders the ciphertext unrecoverable: this is crypto-shredding. It works where overwriting cannot (SSDs with wear leveling, replicated stores). Verification confirms the key is destroyed everywhere it existed. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers key destruction as deletion.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Media-appropriate method selection
description: Sanitization methods are chosen per media type following NIST 800-88 style guidance: Clear, Purge, or Destroy. Magnetic disks, SSDs, and paper each need different methods; the wrong method gives false confidence. Selection is recorded with the deletion receipt. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers Clear/Purge/Destroy per media.
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.

title: Residual data scan
description: After deletion, storage is scanned for remnants: file carving on freed blocks, slack space, and index leftovers. Findings trigger another sanitization pass. Residual scans are the verification that deletion actually deleted. At ladder rank 1 (foundation), this record covers scanning freed blocks and slack space.
demo:
LEVEL = 1
CFG = {1: 100, 2: 1000, 3: 10000}
N = CFG[LEVEL]
import random
random.seed(93)
blocks = [0] * N
blocks[7] = 0xAB  # one remnant
remnants = [i for i, b in enumerate(blocks) if b != 0]
print("scanned:", N, "| remnants:", remnants or ["none"], "| clean:", not remnants)
provenance: Public harvest — documented archive-engineering practice; method fact-checked against standard references.
